author: EmuCore - Hub
title: Prevent accidental touchscreen inputs
summary: Reproduce accidental touch input, identify the active hit region, adjust separation or safe placement one control at a time, and retest grip, gestures, and release.
heroAlt: A mobile-phone capacitive touchscreen with its conductive sensing tracks visible for an accidental-touch diagnosis

sourceLabels.pcsx2-controllers-current: PCSX2 mappings, profiles, ports, and peripherals

blocks.text: Reproduce the unwanted press with the normal grip
Find whether unintended PS2 actions come from overlapping touch targets, palm contact, gesture edges, sticky pointer state, or controls placed under the natural grip.
Making every control smaller can reduce accidental presses while creating missed inputs and inaccessible combinations.

items: Overlay exported before moving or resizing targets.
Touch indicators or a clear in-game response available.
Normal two-handed grip and system gesture mode documented.
1. Repeat the failing grip and action without changing hand position.
2. Identify the exact PS2 control that activates unexpectedly.
3. Lift all fingers and verify that the control returns to neutral.
4. Move the offending target slightly away from the palm or neighbor.
5. Retest intended taps, holds, and slides on that target.
6. Check adjacent controls for new overlap after the move.
7. Repeat near Android back, home, and notification gesture edges.
8. Play a continuous sequence and confirm the correction survives changing grip pressure.

blocks.text: Moving one target or increasing separation tests geometric overlap, whereas changing opacity alone cannot alter the active hit region.
The original grip and action sequence no longer produce unintended controls, while intended presses remain reliable and release cleanly.

items: No unintended target activates during the original reproduction sequence.
Intended presses still register at comfortable thumb positions.
Every touched control releases when the finger leaves its region.

blocks.text: Accidental input patterns needing another cause

items: A control stays held after every finger lifts: diagnose pointer-state or app lifecycle handling.
Only system navigation fires: move away from gesture insets.
Two controls illuminate from one touch: separate overlapping hit regions.
Mispresses appear only while charging: compare touch behavior with the cable removed.

blocks.text: Restore the captured overlay geometry and remove only the failed target adjustment.
Touchscreen hardware can add its own artifacts
A damaged digitizer, low-quality charger, moisture, or screen protector can create ghost touches that no overlay geometry can fully correct.
